terms.gloss: political, to do with public life
evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.6: cīvīlis scientia, political science (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of public life as against private: officia cīvīlia (Quint. 2.15.36). A political career is cursus honōrum (Traupman 180).

evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.12: dē rē pūblicā disputātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Much of what English calls political Latin says with rēs pūblica: talk dē rē pūblicā; for political reasons, reī pūblicae causā (Traupman 180); going into politics, ad rem pūblicam adīre (Cic. Rep. 1.12).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.109: philosophī polīticī (Lewis & Short)
Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.1.5: librī polīticī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek πολιτικός, used of political philosophers and of books on the state.

sources: Lewis & Short: civilis · Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: politicus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. political.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 180.
